groups.label: Writes boilerplate and routine code
groups.definition: The assistant writes boilerplate, repetitive code or routine tickets faster than the developer would.
groups.include: Boilerplate, getters and setters, config files, repetitive code, routine tickets.
groups.exclude: Tests go to 'Drafts tests, fixtures and mock data'; freed time for other work goes to 'Fewer context switches, more time for design'.
groups.rationale: All four cite R01, R08 and R19; A-RQ1-07 adds the boundary at business logic on the same units.

groups.label: Drafts tests, fixtures and mock data
groups.definition: The assistant drafts unit tests, fixtures or mock data, making tests cheaper to start.
groups.include: Unit tests, fixtures, mock data, test coverage.
groups.exclude: Other routine code goes to 'Writes boilerplate and routine code'.
groups.rationale: Three analysts cite R02, R12, R28 with matching definitions.

groups.label: Explains unfamiliar code and error messages
groups.definition: The assistant explains legacy or unfamiliar code and error messages.
groups.include: Summaries and explanations of code, explanations of errors.
groups.exclude: Learning a whole language goes to 'Speeds up learning new languages and frameworks'.

groups.label: Speeds up learning new languages and frameworks
groups.definition: The developer learns a new language or framework faster with the assistant.
groups.include: Picking up a language or framework.
groups.exclude: Explaining a specific piece of code goes to 'Explains unfamiliar code and error messages'.
groups.rationale: R05 and R17 in all three.

groups.label: Writes documentation from notes
groups.definition: The assistant turns the developer's notes into documentation comments.
groups.exclude: Code explanations go to 'Explains unfamiliar code and error messages'.
groups.rationale: Single-unit codes from all three analysts on R22.

groups.label: Fewer context switches, more time for design
groups.definition: The developer stays in context or gains time for higher-level work.
groups.include: No web searches for syntax, time freed for design.
groups.exclude: The kind of code written goes to 'Writes boilerplate and routine code'.
groups.rationale: R26 in all three; A adds R15.

groups.label: Little or no benefit reported
groups.definition: The developer reports little use or less value than expected.
